output.answer: Yes. Oracle is in its second major layoff round of 2026: it began cutting on September 14, 2026, and WARN notices filed that day cover 800 permanent job cuts effective November 13, 2026 (359 in Seattle and 441 across three Bay Area sites). In its Q1 FY2027 10-Q, Oracle disclosed its 2026 Restructuring Plan was estimated at up to $2.1 billion as of August 31, 2026, and was supplemented by roughly $700 million afterward — the cuts come amid heavy AI data-center spending and follow a 21,000-person (13%) workforce decline in fiscal 2026. Oracle has not disclosed a company-wide total for the current round, but a leaked document showed 546 layoffs (about 7.6%) in its America Cloud Infrastructure organization alone.
caveats: Oracle has not publicly confirmed a company-wide headcount for the current round; the 800 figure comes from WARN filings (which cover only Washington and California in that batch) and may not represent the full round of cuts.
The 2,207-worker figure from WARNact aggregates 11 notices filed between May 2025 and September 2026, spanning multiple layoff rounds, not a single announcement.
The $2.1 billion (+$700 million) restructuring total is an estimate ('up to') that Oracle says may change in future results.
WARN notices effective November 13, 2026 are upcoming as of November 11, 2026; details could still shift before the effective date.

passages.quote: During fiscal 2026, our management approved, committed to, initiated and further supplemented plans to restructure to implement certain strategic measures and further improve operational efficiencies, including through the adoption and integration of artificial intelligence technologies across certain functions and other operational activities (2026 Restructuring Plan). The total estimated restructuring costs associated with the 2026 Restructuring Plan are up to $2.1 billion as of August 31, 2026. Subsequent to August 31, 2026, our management supplemented the 2026 Restructuring Plan by approximately $700 million to reflect additional actions that we expect to take. These costs will be recorded to the restructuring and other expense line item within our condensed consolidated statements of operations through the end of the plan. We recorded $167 million and $415 million of restructuring expenses in connection with the 2026 Restructuring Plan for the three months ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Any changes to the estimates of executing the 2026 Restructuring Plan will be reflected in our future results of operations.
passages.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Oracle Form 10-Q, Q1 FY2027)

passages.quote:
"After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change," copies of layoff notification email viewed by Business Insider stated. "As a result, today is your last working day."

Employees [were offered](https://www.businessinsider.com/oracle-severance-package-us-employees-2026-9) 4 weeks' base salary plus 1 week per year of employment, according to documents viewed by Business Insider.

Cloud computing giant Oracle is laying off more employees this week as it extends a multibillion-dollar restructuring plan. The job cuts include 359 in Seattle, according to a regulatory filing Wednesday.

The Austin, Texas-based company disclosed in an annual regulatory filing earlier this year that its total workforce decreased by roughly 21,000 employees from 2025, costing the company about $2.1 billion, mostly through severance packages and contract terminations.

Those cuts affected 741 Seattle-area employees between August 2025 and March, which, coupled with this week’s layoffs, means 1,100 Oracle workers in Seattle have been let go since last summer.

In a quarterly regulatory filing, Oracle addressed its 2026 restructuring plan and said it took further action after the fiscal quarter ended on Aug. 31, costing an additional $700 million and causing this week’s layoffs.

Oracle Corporation filed four WARN notices dated Sept. 14, 2026, reporting 800 permanent job cuts effective Nov. 13, 2026 across Washington and California. The notices list 359 workers in Seattle and 441 across three Bay Area sites (279 in Redwood City, 99 in Santa Clara and 63 in Pleasanton). The filings do not state a reason for the cuts and Oracle provided no statement in the article. The article notes these WARN notices were filed before recent reports about Oracle's AI cloud contracts and emphasizes the notices cover only Washington and California so they may not represent the company's full round of cuts.

It shows the job titles and ages of 546 employees in Oracle's America Cloud Infrastructure organization who were laid off, representing around 7.6% of the 7,185 employees listed. Of those, managers, engineers, software developers, and workers in the company's data center maintenance and servicing division were most affected.

Oracle said in the document that the information was provided to comply with federal age discrimination laws.

It provides an insight into the type of roles the company is eliminating in its [second major round](https://www.businessinsider.com/read-oracle-layoff-email-employees-job-cuts-2026-3) of job cuts this year. Oracle has not said how many people it laid off in total last week.

The document states that it includes all employees in Oracle America's Cloud Infrastructure organization eligible to receive severance benefits.

key_facts.fact: Oracle began a new (second major of 2026) round of layoffs on September 14, 2026, confirmed by impacted employees and a layoff notification email; US employees were offered 4 weeks' base salary plus 1 week per year of service.

Oracle filed four WARN notices dated September 14, 2026 reporting 800 permanent job cuts effective November 13, 2026: 359 in Seattle and 441 across three Bay Area sites (279 Redwood City, 99 Santa Clara, 63 Pleasanton).

Oracle's Q1 FY2027 10-Q states total estimated 2026 Restructuring Plan costs of up to $2.1 billion as of August 31, 2026, supplemented by approximately $700 million after quarter-end; $167 million of restructuring expense was recorded in the quarter ended August 31, 2026.
Bloomberg reported September 11, 2026 that Oracle increased the scale of its planned job cuts (an additional $700 million) amid a cash crunch tied to AI data-center development.
Oracle's workforce declined by 21,000 employees, or 13%, in fiscal 2026 (ended May 31, 2026); Oracle had about 141,000 employees before the September 2026 round.

A leaked document shows 546 employees laid off in Oracle's America Cloud Infrastructure organization, about 7.6% of the 7,185 listed, hitting managers, engineers, software developers and data-center maintenance roles hardest.

WARN trackers show 11 Oracle WARN notices across 5 states affecting 2,207 workers, with filing dates from May 7, 2025 through September 14, 2026; the September 2026 notices (Seattle 359, Pleasanton 63, Redwood City 279, Santa Clara 99) all take effect November 13, 2026.

Oracle said in a filing earlier in 2026 that 'the adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce'; 1,100 Seattle Oracle workers have been let go since summer 2025.
